rv-be:inventory:1.note: still visible in code: InventoryStockDomainService.processEntry (~l.342-350), consumeInTransitLine (~l.191), createOrFindBalance/addOnHandOnly read the balance without a lock; no @Version on InventoryBalance/ChannelAllocation. Only the sales item-receive path now locks (ItemReceiveDomainService ~l.355 via findOrCreateByDimensionForUpdate); bin transfer, adjustment and packing house handlers do not.
rv-be:inventory:1.summary: Stock quantities (on hand, reserved) are read, changed and saved without locking the row. Two requests on the same item and bin at the same moment both start from the same number, so the second save overwrites the first. The result is lost stock, or the last 10 units reserved twice. Anyone moving or receiving stock in parallel is affected, and valuation and accounting postings inherit the wrong quantity.
steps: Pick an item with 10 on hand in one bin and no reservation.
Send two simultaneous POST /api/inventory/bin-transfers requests (workflow active, so quantity is reserved) each moving 10 from that bin.
Read GET /api/inventory/items/{itemId}/inventory-balance.
rv-be:inventory:1.expected: Exactly one request reserves the 10 units; the second is refused with 400 because nothing is free.
rv-be:inventory:1.actual: Both can pass the free-quantity check (read before either commit), so reserved can reach 20 against 10 on hand; two parallel receipts can also end with the quantity of only one.
rv-be:inventory:1.where: backend inventory/stock/service/InventoryStockDomainService (processEntry, consumeInTransitLine, createOrFindBalance, addOnHandOnly); transfer/handler/BinTransferWorkflowHandler.moveStockToDestination; adjustment/handler/InventoryAdjustmentWorkflowHandler; packing_house/service/PackingHouseBookDomainService; InventoryBalanceRepository.findByItemIdAndDimensionIdForUpdate exists but is unused here
rv-be:inventory:1.verify: Run the two-parallel-request step 2 (script with two concurrent HTTP calls). After the fix exactly one succeeds and reserved_qty never exceeds on_hand_qty.
